newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France wants 25 bln francs from Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France wants 25 bln francs from Telecom sale.

text.p: France said on Monday it hoped to raise 25 billion francs ($4.91 billion) from the sale next April of a minority stake in state-owned France Telecom in what is expected to the country's biggest-ever privatisation.
The float is one of a raft of share offerings in Europe by state-controlled telecoms operators in the countdown to the 1998 liberalisation of the European telecommunications market.
The sale is targeted to take place between mid-April and mid-June next year, a finance ministry spokesman said.
"The government hopes to raise 25 billion francs from the sale," he said.
The sales will follow the November 17 flotation of Germany's giant Deutsche Telekom -- Europe's largest offering -- worth $10 billion.
The flotation of Italy's state telecoms group, Stet, expected to be worth $8 billion, is not likely to come to market before late 1997.

The partial sale of France Telecom is likely to be made in two tranches. Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said last month that 20 percent would be sold off in the first tranche, but the finance spokesman said on Monday the amount had not been fixed.
"It could be 20 percent but we don't know yet. It depends on a multitude of factors," he said, declining to elaborate. The timing of the second tranche's sale was not decided, he said.
The government has pledged to keep a 51 percent holding with an extra maximum 10 percent set aside for the workforce.
The 25 billion francs would largely meet the government's goal of raising 27 billion francs from privatisation receipts next year, the finance spokesman said.
The money is expected to be used for capital injections to make ready for sale other state-owned firms on the centre-right government's privatisation list, such as ailing bank Credit Lyonnais.

On Friday, the ministry named two French banks, Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) and Banque Paribas as global coordinators of the float, a move seen as a sign it wanted to ensure strong domestic French demand for the offering.
Fillon said last month the government wanted to "carry out the largest public offering in France" and pointed to France Telecom's 32 million customers as "a fantastic starting point".
The government wanted to "be at least as ambitious as Deutche Telekom, which is aiming for two million individual shareholders", he said.
Analysts say a successful Deutsche Telekom flotation could bode well for issues to come later such as France Telecom.
The ministry said the sale would include both a public sale as well as a private placement with institutional investors.

France Telecom is currently valued at between 100 and 200 billion francs. The big range is partly because details have yet to be agreed on interconnection charges for new operators when the French telecoms market is opened to competition in 1998.

The ministry spokesman would not put a more specific value on the company. Last July, financial analysts at Barclays de Zoete Wedd assigned France Telecom a value of 147 billion francs. They said they expected group profits to increase around 10.7 percent a year over the next five years.
France Telecom recorded 1995 profits of 9.2 billion francs on sales of 147.8 billion.
France Telecom is to be transformed into a limited company on January 1, 1997, paving the way for its flotation. ($1=5.087 French Franc)
